key_concepts.summary: S&C supports boxing skill; it should not replace technical training.
Sparring/contact exposure must be tracked separately from gym, bag, and conditioning load.
Aerobic capacity supports between-burst and between-round recovery.
Punching power training should use quality reps, rest, and force-transfer logic, not fatigue circuits.
General prep, specific camp, sparring peak, taper, fight week, and post-fight recovery require different prescriptions.
Headache, dizziness, poor sleep, high stress, or hand pain should reduce contact intensity before reducing only gym work.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not prescribe hard sparring as a default workout; require coach context and readiness.
Progress contact only after stance, guard, defense, and controlled partner drills are stable.
Place speed/power work before fatigue conditioning or on separate days.
Avoid heavy neck/shoulder fatigue immediately before high-contact sparring.
The day after high-contact or high-intensity sparring should bias recovery, low-contact skill, or low-fatigue aerobic work.
Avoid dehydration protocols; use safe body-composition planning and professional referral for aggressive cuts.

physical_demands.quality: supports repeated round recovery and training volume
supports explosive exchanges and late-round output
supports punches from hips/trunk into shoulders and hands
supports posture, impact tolerance context, and force transfer
supports guard, punching volume, and defense
supports movement, angles, and stance endurance

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Sparring and competition include head-impact risk; symptoms should stop contact and trigger medical review.
Punching impact can overload hand/wrist, especially with poor technique or wrapping.
Repeated punching and guard fatigue can overload shoulder/scapular structures.
Neck fatigue or contact load can raise risk during sparring.
High rotational volume with poor hip/trunk control can irritate the back.
Aggressive weight loss can impair recovery, cognition, and performance.

training_implications.summary: Track skill, contact, conditioning, and strength loads separately.
Use roadwork, intervals, bag circuits, and non-contact drills to condition without excess head contact.
Add neck isometrics, scapular control, trunk anti-rotation, and shoulder capacity as appropriate.
Sparring should build then taper; it should not rise endlessly into fight week.
After competition, prioritize medical clearance, symptoms, tissue recovery, and gradual re-entry.
